textbook:
Clean cutaway textbook illustration of a SINGLE norovirus particle (Caliciviridae, the stomach-bug virus), drawn as a THREE-DIMENSIONAL BALL seen from outside in three-quarter view, centered and large in a square 1:1 1080x1080 frame with empty negative space around it for later labels. House style: semi-flat vector-style shading with THIN, CRISP, CLEAN dark outlines (never heavy black cartoon strokes), every structure carrying its own DISTINCT, CLEARLY READABLE soft colour fill with gentle soft shading — refined and elegant, not washed-out, not pastel-faded, not low-contrast. Muted, sophisticated, slightly desaturated educational palette (soft dusty tints, never bright primary or cartoon colours) on a neutral dark charcoal uncluttered background that fills the frame edge-to-edge — no border, no frame, no vignette, no outer glow or white halo around the particle, no sheet lying on a surface.

SURFACE — this is the whole point of the picture, get it exactly right:
The virion is a NAKED, NON-ENVELOPED capsid: one single continuous protein ball. Its surface is sculpted, like a raspberry or a hand-thrown clay ball, in two alternating features:
(1) NINETY low ARCHING MOUNDS that SWELL OUT OF the ball itself. Each mound is one VP1 dimer: an elongated, smoothly rounded ridge, roughly the shape of an almond lying on its side, whose base flows seamlessly into the shell — the same material, not a separate flat disc or pill laid on top. They are packed tightly against each other, in pairs, in an icosahedral arrangement. Nothing has a stem, stalk, neck, pedestal, mushroom cap, club, T-shape or knob-on-a-stick; NOTHING projects away from the ball on a support. Fill each mound desaturated sage-teal along its base and clear dusty rose over its raised crest, with a thin crisp outline separating it from its neighbours.
(2) THIRTY-TWO round BOWL-SHAPED HOLLOWS scooped BETWEEN the mounds — twelve at the five-fold vertices, twenty at the three-fold positions — so that roughly a dozen of them are visible on the face turned toward us. Each must read unmistakably CONCAVE: a shallow saucer scooped into the surface, with a crescent of deep indigo-grey shadow banked against its far inner wall and a lighter muted slate periwinkle-blue floor curving away below it. They are DEPRESSIONS, closed at the bottom: NOT rings, NOT doughnuts, NOT flat discs, NOT lenses, NOT bulging domes, NOT holes bored through the shell, NOT tunnels, NOT eyes. These cups gave the calicivirus family its name.
In silhouette the rim of the particle must read gently SCALLOPED, bumpy and cauliflower-like — never spiky, never fringed, never a corona, never a smooth circle.

INTERIOR — cut ONE clean wedge, about a fifth of the ball, out of the upper right so the interior is generously readable; the rest of the ball stays whole and intact. The cut faces show the shell as ONE single thin layer only. Inside the hollow, on a dark muted interior: a single long continuous coppery-orange single-stranded RNA thread, coiled loosely and IRREGULARLY like a length of string dropped into a bowl, with uneven loops of different sizes going in different directions. It must NEVER be drawn as a regular spring, a coiled helix, a corkscrew, a spiral of even pitch, a zigzag or two parallel lines — one irregular tangled thread only, and only ONE of them. A small deep-indigo bead (the VPg protein) sits attached to one free end of that thread. Three or four pale ochre-mustard VP2 protein blobs lie tucked against the inner face of the shell.

Do NOT draw any lipid envelope, membrane bilayer or greasy halo; NO stalked spikes, clubs, mushrooms or fuzzy fringe of any kind; NO double helix or DNA; NO segmented or multiple RNA pieces; NO second or third concentric shell layer; NO rotavirus-style triple-layered wheel; NO polymerase; NO matrix layer; NO nucleoprotein beads along the RNA; no organelles, no cell wall, no phage tail or legs, no face. Anatomically faithful, one specimen only. Absolutely NO text, letters, numbers, labels, scale bars, arrows or watermarks in the image.
